react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on two tightly linked metabolic modules. The dominant signal is Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043), the top-ranked pathway in both RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 1.65 × 10⁻¹², fold-enrichment ≈ 1 090) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (raw p = 5.16 × 10⁻⁸). Mummichog's empirical-compound network independently recovers the same module as the 5th-ranked hit (p = 0.0029). Five input metabolites map to this pathway across all three methods: galactitol, myo-inositol, sucrose, α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol (galactinol), and glycerol. Galactitol and galactinol are galactose-pathway-specific metabolites whose simultaneous differential abundance is the hallmark of perturbed galactose catabolism. myo-Inositol and glycerol function as downstream or alternative-route intermediates, tying the galactose cluster to osmolyte and energy metabolism. A second coherent cluster centres on glycerophospholipid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00561 / MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism / REACT:R-HSA-1483206), detected by RaMP ORA (FDR 2.48 × 10⁻⁵), Mummichog (#2, p = 0.0015), and MetaboAnalystR (p = 0.078). The driver metabolites — glycerol, choline, myo-inositol, and O-phosphoethanolamine — are canonical glycerophospholipid head-group precursors, implying phospholipid biosynthesis or remodelling is concurrently affected. Together, the two modules suggest the treatment perturbation drives both a specific block or diversion of galactose catabolism and a broader glycerophospholipid biosynthetic response. Guanabenz and butan-2-one were not represented in either pathway cluster, consistent with their roles as xenobiotic effector (α₂-adrenergic agonist) and a ketogenic intermediate, respectively.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant pathway disturbance in the treatment group. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA returns Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) and Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052) both at rank 0-2 with FDR 1.65e-12, driven by galactitol, myo-inositol, sucrose, galactinol and glycerol. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms the same pathway (hsa00052) at rank 0 with p-value 5.16e-08, sharing the identical five hit metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment returns Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) at rank 4 (p=0.00185) with a 10-metabolite overlap. A secondary cross-paradigm signal emerges in glycerophospholipid metabolism: RaMP hits the Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP:WP2533, FDR 2.48e-05) and Glycerophospholipid biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1483206, FDR 1.21e-04), while mummichog independently recovers Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, p=0.00101). Three driver metabolites — galactitol, sucrose and galactinol — are confirmed members of the Galactose Metabolism module; myo-inositol additionally functions as the head-group donor in Glycerophospholipid pathways. Guanabenz, butanone, 2-ketobutyric acid and O-phosphoethanolamine are flagged as noise metabolites absent from both primary pathway hit rosters.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on two tightly linked metabolic modules. The dominant signal is Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043), the top-ranked pathway in both RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 1.65 × 10⁻¹², fold-enrichment ≈ 1 090) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (raw p = 5.16 × 10⁻⁸). Mummichog's empirical-compound network independently recovers the same module as the 5th-ranked hit (p = 0.0029). Five input metabolites map to this pathway across all three methods: galactitol, myo-inositol, sucrose, α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol (galactinol), and glycerol. Galactitol and galactinol are galactose-pathway-specific metabolites whose simultaneous differential abundance is the hallmark of perturbed galactose catabolism. myo-Inositol and glycerol function as downstream or alternative-route intermediates, tying the galactose cluster to osmolyte and energy metabolism. A second coherent cluster centres on glycerophospholipid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00561 / MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism / REACT:R-HSA-1483206), detected by RaMP ORA (FDR 2.48 × 10⁻⁵), Mummichog (#2, p = 0.0015), and MetaboAnalystR (p = 0.078). The driver metabolites — glycerol, choline, myo-inositol, and O-phosphoethanolamine — are canonical glycerophospholipid head-group precursors, implying phospholipid biosynthesis or remodelling is concurrently affected. Together, the two modules suggest the treatment perturbation drives both a specific block or diversion of galactose catabolism and a broader glycerophospholipid biosynthetic response. Guanabenz and butan-2-one were not represented in either pathway cluster, consistent with their roles as xenobiotic effector (α₂-adrenergic agonist) and a ketogenic intermediate, respectively.
